name: Bean Angular Leaf Spot
description: A fungal disease causing characteristic angular gray lesions on bean leaves. It is favored by cool, wet conditions and causes premature defoliation, leading to significant yield reduction.
symptoms: Angular gray to brown lesions delimited by leaf veins
Lesions visible on both leaf surfaces
Dark gray fungal growth on lesion undersides
Leaves turning yellow and dropping prematurely
causes: Extended leaf wetness from rain or heavy dew
Dense planting with poor air circulation
treatments: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb
Spray copper-based fungicides at first symptoms
prevention: Space plants adequately for air circulation
Practice crop rotation with non-legume crops
